summary: Cab removed after the Pinery tower closed, but the structure still stands; while active it was visible from the park's main gate.

facts.status_note: Cab removed after the tower closed; the structure still stands (Firelookout.ca).

evidence.supports: Pinery Provincial Park is on Lake Huron in Bosanquet Township, Lambton County, about 6 km south of Grand Bend
evidence.quote: Pinery Provincial Park, 2532.5 hectares in size, is located on the southeast shore of Lake Huron in Bosanquet Township, Lambton County, approximately 6 kilometres south of Grand Bend on Highway No. 21

evidence.supports: while active the tower could be seen from the park's main gate
evidence.quote: This tower, when active, could be seen from the main gate of the Pinery Provincial Park.

evidence.supports: after closure the cab was removed; the structure still stands
evidence.quote: Since its closure, its cab has been removed, but it still stands.

evidence.supports: most Ontario towers erected 1920s to 1950s, in forest fire protection's heyday
evidence.quote: Most of the towers were erected between the 1920's and the 1950's when forest fire protection was in it's heyday.

evidence.supports: from the 1960s aerial spotting and firefighting crews took over; towers used less
evidence.quote: As the 1960's progressed the towers were in use less and less as aerial fire spotting and fire fighting crews took over.

evidence.supports: the MNR decided in 2013 to remove many standing towers; the fan site does not name the Pinery tower
evidence.quote: The Ontario MNR has decided, as of 2013, to remove many of these towers still standing.

sources.title: Ontario's Fire Tower Lookouts: Preserving Their History

notes_for_editor: Thin evidence: one tower-specific Firelookout.ca entry (closure and cab removal, no year) plus the Ontario park plan for the park's location. The brief's local_unit (Lambton County) matches the park plan, which places the park in Bosanquet Township, Lambton County; the Firelookout.ca address field also reads 'Lambton Shores, Lambton County'; the story names the county only for the park. Firelookout.ca shows '212 m (696 ft)' on the page, which the brief records as elevation_m; that is not structure height, so height_m is not set and the figure is not in the story. No closure date, staffing or fire history was found. Two sources disagree on who bought the park land in 1957 (Wikipedia says the Canada Company; a Grand Bend archive page says the Government of Canada). Not needed for the tower story and not used. Access is left unset: the Firelookout.ca entry does not say whether the tower is open to visitors.
